text:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: kv_cache_eviction_spike + streaming_cadence_drop on prod-us-east-1. firing since 04:12 UTC. links: https://incidents/internal/2001234567

marta: seeing same. dashboards show KV cache size + eviction_rate up 10x, tail latency for streaming requests spiking. triage in this thread.

kevin: quick context — we rolled continuous_batcher v2 yesterday (rollout at 02:40). suspect change to `continuous_batch_window_ms` and `prefix_cache_ttl` interaction. might be causing many tiny batches + cache churn.

deepa: logs from node-03 show repeated warming writes: `prefix_cache:insert key=usr_pref_*, size=48MB, ttl=2592000` but TTL unexpectedly set high for ephemeral prefixes. eviction_count keeps climbing. snippet:```
[04:10:12] KVCache:size=2.3GB eviction_count=4521 alloc=1.9GB
[04:11:09] KVCache:insert key=usr_pref_abc123 size=12KB ttl=2592000
[04:11:09] continuous_batcher:flush batch_id=xyz cadence_ms=0
```

sam: also seeing streaming cadence stalls on those same nodes — tokens are produced but `partial_flush` not triggering if `kv_cache_evict_inflight` is true. results in stalls ~800-1200ms. hypothesis: eviction path holds locks that block cadence timer.

marta: impact? which customers? severity?

jess: CS pinged — 2 paying customers (cust-1843, cust-992) reported timeouts on chat streaming starting ~04:15. ETA to respond depends on fix. customers on Dedicated pools in us-east-1.

kevin: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily reduce `continuous_batch_window_ms` to 8ms from 25ms to reduce tiny-batch amplification. 2) lower `continuous_batch_max_tokens` to 512 -> 128. 3) disable prefix caching for model `text-redwood-2` on effected pools only. That should reduce writes to KV and stop eviction storm.

marta: I can patch config via control plane. will do canary to 10% of nodes first. running command now.```bash
# patch runtime config for pool us-east-1
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/pools/us-east-1/config \
  -d '{"continuous_batch_window_ms":8,"continuous_batch_max_tokens":128,"prefix_caching_mode":"disabled"}'
```

ops-bot: deploy started by marta. rollout id: r-2001-canary. 10% nodes targeted. status: in_progress.

sam: good. also add a temporary throttle on prefix_warm_writes to avoid immediate rebuild: `prefix_warm_rate_limit=10/s`.

marta: added that too, resent patch.```bash
# throttle warm writes
curl -X POST ... -d '{"prefix_warm_rate_limit":10}'
```

ops-bot: canary rolled out -> 2 nodes updated. health checks passed. status: partial_rollout_ok.

deepa: after canary metrics: eviction_count down on canary nodes from ~1200/min to ~30/min. KV size stable. streaming token latency on canary nodes reduced from p95 1.2s -> 180ms. logs:```
[04:26:01] node-07 KVCache: eviction_count=28 size=530MB
[04:26:06] continuous_batcher: cadence_ms=6 flushes=120/s
[04:26:07] streaming:token_latency_p95=180ms
```

kevin: looks promising. plan: scale rollout to 60% over next 10m, monitor. I will open a hotfix PR to fix the TTL assignment for ephemeral prefixes and add safer defaults. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pull/7812

sam: for streaming partial flush bug — I have a small patch to force `partial_flush` when `tokens_in_flight>0 && inflight_evictions>0` so we don't deadlock waiting for eviction locks. will include in the same hotfix page but want canary for that too.

marta: rolling to 60% now. ops-bot updates: rollout id r-2001-phase2.

ops-bot: rollout 60% complete. health_ok.

jess: CS update — latency/error rates dropped for cust-1843 and cust-992 after canary. they will watch, asked for status email.

deepa: note: while this mitigates, root cause is TTL regression from model-warming job that sets prefix TTL to 30 days for ephemeral prefixes. I'll add a regression test.

kevin: timeline/impact note for postmortem:
- 02:40 deploy continuous_batcher v2 (config change)
- 04:10 first eviction spike alert
- 04:14 customers report timeouts
- 04:20 mitigations applied (canary)
- 04:26 canary metrics improved
- 04:35 rollout to 60% -> stable

sam: streaming partial_flush patch queued as hotfix + unit tests, PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pull/7816. will canary with smaller batch window first.

marta: full rollout to 100% starting in 5m. will keep throttles in place until TTL fix lands.

ops-bot: rollout 100% complete at 04:42. post-rollout health checks: p99 latency back to baseline, error_rate reduced to normal.

deepa: quick before/after stats:```
METRIC, before, after
kv_eviction_rate, 1200/min, 22/min
kv_size_total, 2.3GB, 640MB
streaming_token_latency_p95, 1.2s, 170ms
customer_timeouts, 18/min, 0/min
```

jess: sending customers a short update. phrasing: "We observed increased streaming latency and timeouts due to cache churn on us-east-1; mitigations applied and we're rolling a permanent fix. We'll follow up with RCA."

kevin: severity: Sev2 (customer-visible degradation, partial outage for a small set of Dedicated pools). Follow-ups:
- fix TTL regression (PR 7812) + tests
- partial_flush race analysis (PR 7816) + deeper lock profiling
- add alert for continuous_batch_window anomalies
- add canary gating for batcher config changes

marta: handing off to night on-call @kevin for follow-ups. Kevin, please pick up RCA, tests, and verify PRs. I'll add notes to incident doc and assign tasks.

kevin: ack. I'll keep this thread updated. thanks team. :thumbsup:

marta: incident closed to active response. tracking follow-ups in https://issues/internal/RED-2879. Handoff done at 04:58 UTC.
